result.name: typed-correctness: daily values as first-class types, hooks with checked protocols
result.overview:
Orientation: the daily quantity becomes a named type in the shape system, every operator family's right to consume it is decided by a shape rule and raised in `make_node`, and every hook validates its own contract at construction time rather than failing at the first draw.

Four load-bearing facts I verified live (read-only, `PYTHONPATH=/Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube/src ~/.venvs/alphacube/bin/python`), because they decide the shape of the design:

1. A new leaf class is NOT a leaf to the DAG. `Node.is_leaf` is `isinstance(self.expr, (Feature, Constant))` (/Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube/src/alphacube/engine/dag.py:39-40), so a new class lands in `dag.computed`, and `plan_rounds` -> `assign_modes` -> `_p_eligible` dies on `spec.face` with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'face'`. Widening that tuple is mandatory, not cosmetic.
2. With `is_leaf` fixed, a COLLAPSED-shaped daily leaf is routed into PANEL rounds by the existing scheduler, and the panel round has no loader for it. `div(day_sum(Amt), FloatCap)` plans as `S[1] -> P[1]` with the `div` node in MODE_P; `cs_rank(FloatCap)` and `ts_delay(FloatCap, 1)` are pure-P. `_run_panel_round.operand` (engine.py:356-363) handles only `Constant`, `values` and `panels`, so all three raise `RuntimeError("panel operand DF:FloatCap unavailable")`. This is the gap a design that only patches `_load_leaf_cube` will miss.
3. Cube-mode exposure is real too: `day_mean(div(Amt, FloatCap))` plans as one S round with no boundary, so `_load_leaf_cube` must hand back `(A, B, 1)`; and `cross_mean(FloatCap, 5)` reaches the per-stock D-axis loop in S mode.
4. A bare daily leaf as root reaches `_leaf_panel` (engine.py:208-216), which raises `ValueError("leaf ... is not a daily value")` -- `evaluate()` only gates on `shape.degenerate`, which a daily leaf satisfies.

Design decisions that follow from the typed-correctness brief:

- The daily leaf's shape is `COLLAPSED`'s structure (collapsed, degenerate, width=1) plus one new flag, `daily_only`. Reusing the structure is the typed-correct answer -- two values of the same type must be interchangeable, and once materialised a daily field and a `day_*` output are identical `(A,B,1)` tensors, with the exact same round-boundary handling. The new flag exists for the one place where they are NOT interchangeable: `operand_ok`'s legacy carve-out `(not strict) and spec.reduces_m and sh.collapsed` would silently make `day_sum(FloatCap)` the identity under `parse_legacy`. The flag closes that in every mode, with a message, while leaving `day_sum(day_mean(Close))` exactly as it is.
- `daily_only` propagates by `all()` over operands, so no tree reachable without a daily leaf changes value, and a mixed tree (`div(day_mean(Close), FloatCap)`) keeps today's legacy behaviour. This buys byte-identity at the cost of completeness; see risks.
- Hooks validate at construction: an operator-weight key that names no operator, a negative or NaN weight, a weight set that empties any producer bucket, a non-callable or wrong-arity accept hook, a scorer factory that cannot take `**kwargs`, a scorer name shadowing a built-in -- each raises from `__init__`/`register_scorer`, not from the 400th generated tree.
- The plugin entry point is an explicit `register_alphacube(ctx)`, not import side effects, and `catalog.build_registry` latches the operator registry closed afterwards so "registered too late" is a loud `RuntimeError` instead of silently-missing operators. AlphaCube never imports Partura; the only coupling is a module-name string on `--plugin`.

TYPE SYSTEM -- /Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube/src/alphacube/expression.py

`Shape` gains a fourth field, keyword-defaulted so every existing construction is unchanged:

    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class Shape:
        collapsed: bool
        degenerate: bool
        width: Optional[int] = None
        daily_only: bool = False      # defined only per (stock, day): there is no minute axis to reduce or roll over

    FULL            = Shape(collapsed=False, degenerate=False)
    COLLAPSED       = Shape(collapsed=True,  degenerate=True, width=1)
    WIDE_DEGENERATE = Shape(collapsed=False, degenerate=True)
    DAILY           = Shape(collapsed=True,  degenerate=True, width=1, daily_only=True)

`DAILY != COLLAPSED` under dataclass equality, so `tests/test_expression.py::test_shape_typing`'s table (which asserts `day_*` outputs `== COLLAPSED`) is untouched. `Shape` is constructed only inside expression.py and never positionally beyond three args (grep-verified).

New leaf class, next to `Feature`:

    class DailyFeature(Expression):
        __slots__ = ("field",)
        def __init__(self, field: str) -> None: self.field = field
        def _make_key(self) -> str: return f"DF:{self.field}"       # never collides with F:<field>
        def _infer_shape(self) -> Shape: return DAILY
        def _repr(self) -> str: return self.field

A separate class rather than `Feature(field, daily=True)`: `isinstance(n, Feature)` is read by `is_valid_root` (expression.py:404), `parser.daily_of` (parser.py:254), `mining/clustering.py:30`, `mining/boosting.py:157`, `mining/alphasage.py:39`. The `DF:` key tag matters because `key()` is the sole identity for CSE (engine/dag.py:61), GP population dedup and ban lookups (mining/gp.py), the mutation env (mining/env.py) and seed dedup (mining/boosting.py) -- a daily `FloatCap` and a hypothetical minute field of the same name must never share a cache slot.

Shared leaf tuple, exported so dag.py/engine.py use one definition instead of three:

    LEAF_TYPES = (Feature, Constant, DailyFeature)

`operand_ok` gains one rule, FIRST, before `restores_m`:

        return False      # no mode, strict or legacy

and `_why_not` gains the matching message ("`{name}` ({face}/{family}) rolls or reduces over the minute axis; `{operand!r}` has no minute axis (it is a daily value)"). Verified behaviour table for the new leaf (`needs_full_m` = `(face=='dt' and family in ('in','day')) or face=='nt'`, axes.py:89-91):

    in_*    dt/in    strict REJECT  legacy REJECT   (unchanged)
    nt_*    nt/*     strict REJECT  legacy REJECT   (unchanged)
    in_expand        strict ACCEPT  legacy ACCEPT   -- deliberate: an explicit widening; its output is WIDE_DEGENERATE

    cs_*/ts_* nd/*   ACCEPT (needs_daily only asks degenerate)

A separate module, not store.py's `build_cube_store`: that function enforces `len({cubes[n].shape}) == 1` and `CubeStore.field()` asserts `(n_symbols, n_days, n_minutes)` per field, so a `(S, D)` array cannot live in a minute store without weakening both invariants. The format follows the precedent `scripts/compare_daily_store.py:130-152` already reads -- the V2 `daily/` layout -- with the same alignment contract:

    class DailyFieldStore:
        """<root>/daily_fields/: field_<name>.npy (D_all, S_all) float32 + meta.json
        {schema_version, dates: [...], symbols: [...], fields: [...], built_at, source, cap_dir}.

        The store spans every date and instrument ever ingested; a view is a window
        into it. Alignment is BY LABEL, never by position."""
        fields: List[str]; dates: List[str]; symbols: List[str]; contract_hash: str
        def panel(self, name: str, dates: Sequence[str], symbols: Sequence[str]) -> np.ndarray:
            """(len(symbols), len(dates)) float32 -- (S, D), the engine's internal orientation.
            Raises KeyError naming the first date the store does not cover (a view whose
            warm-up reaches before the store's first date must fail loudly, not silently
            return NaN). A symbol the store does not list becomes a NaN column, counted."""
        def coverage(self, name: str) -> Dict[str, float]      # finite share, missing-symbol count

The transpose from the stored `(D, S)` to the returned `(S, D)` happens exactly once, here. That is deliberate: four orientations are live in this codebase (raw parquet and `tradability.board_limit` are (D,S); the engine's internal `panels` dict is (S,D), engine.py:151; `EvalResult.panels` is (D,S) via one `p.T` at engine.py:196; P-round tensors are (D,S)), and a transpose bug produces a plausible panel, not a crash.

    def daily_s(self, name, s_lo, s_hi) -> np.ndarray:     # (C, D) -- a slice of the cache
    def daily_d(self, name, d_lo, d_hi) -> np.ndarray:     # (S, C) -- a slice of the cache

1. SCORER REGISTRY -- /Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube/src/alphacube/mining/scoring.py

    _SCORER_FACTORIES: Dict[str, Callable[..., Any]] = {}

    def register_scorer(name: str, factory: Callable[..., Any], *, replace: bool = False) -> None:
        """``factory(target, **kw) -> scorer`` with ``.score(panel, gated=True) -> {..., 'fit': float}``,
        ``.score_combined(panel)`` and optionally ``.columns`` (extra archive columns).

        ``kw`` carries turnover_penalty / signed / cost_per_side / top_frac / min_coverage /
        min_scored_days AND ``dates`` -- the view's date strings, ROW-ALIGNED with the panels
        and the target the scorer is handed, warm-up rows included -- so a factory can cut its
        own train/valid. A factory must accept **kwargs; it will be given keys it does not know."""

    def scorer_kinds() -> Tuple[str, ...]: return FITNESS_KINDS + tuple(sorted(_SCORER_FACTORIES))

Validated at registration, not at first use: `name` a non-empty identifier; not shadowing `FITNESS_KINDS` unless `replace=True`; `callable(factory)`; and `inspect.signature(factory)` must accept one positional parameter plus `**kwargs` (a factory with a fixed keyword list silently breaks the first time a new kwarg is added) -- each otherwise `TypeError`/`ValueError`.

                    top_frac=BOOK_TOP_FRAC, min_coverage=0.5, min_scored_days=0.5,

2. GENERATOR HOOKS -- /Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube/src/alphacube/mining/generator.py

`TypedTreeGenerator.__init__` gains three keyword parameters:

    operator_weights: Optional[Mapping[str, float]] = None,   # name -> relative weight; an absent name is 1.0
    accept_hook: Optional[Callable[[Expression], bool]] = None,
    mutation_checks_bans: bool = True,

Construction-time validation (the typed-correctness payoff: a bad weight set is a `ValueError` from `__init__`, not an `IndexError` from `_pick` 400 trees later):
  - every key must be in `registry`, else `ValueError(f"operator_weights: no operator named {k!r}")`;
  - every value a finite float >= 0, else `ValueError`;
  - after dropping weight-0 operators, each `self._producers` bucket that is non-empty today must stay non-empty, AND `[s for s in self.specs if s.reduces_m and not s.non_root]` must stay non-empty. This is the real failure mode: zeroing every `reduces_m` operator makes `_gen("daily", 1, ...)` raise `ShapeError` forever and `generate()`'s fallback `self._collapse_leaf(self._pick(self._root_ops_of("reduce")))` reach `self._rng.choice(sorted({}))`;
  - `accept_hook` must be callable with exactly one positional parameter, else `TypeError`.

`_pick`, rewritten so the unweighted path keeps exactly two `random.Random.choice` calls in the same order with the same arguments:

    def _pick(self, specs: List[OpSpec]) -> OpSpec:
        faces: Dict[str, List[OpSpec]] = {}
        for s in specs:
            faces.setdefault(s.face, []).append(s)
        if self._weights is None:
            return self._rng.choice(faces[self._rng.choice(sorted(faces))])   # byte-identical to today
        wf = {f: [(s, self._weights.get(s.name, 1.0)) for s in pool] for f, pool in faces.items()}
        wf = {f: [(s, w) for s, w in pool if w > 0] for f, pool in wf.items()}
        wf = {f: pool for f, pool in wf.items() if pool}
        if not wf:                                   # every candidate in THIS slot has weight 0
            return self._rng.choice(faces[self._rng.choice(sorted(faces))])   # documented fallback
        names = sorted(wf)
        f = self._rng.choices(names, weights=[sum(w for _, w in wf[n]) / len(wf[n]) for n in names])[0]
        return self._rng.choices([s for s, _ in wf[f]], weights=[w for _, w in wf[f]])[0]

The weighted path draws through `random.choices`, a different consumption of the same Mersenne stream -- which is the point, and is reached only when a caller passes weights. Face selection by mean operator weight matches what Partura's monkeypatch does today, so the migration is behaviour-preserving for it.

`acceptable`, with the hook at the same acceptance point as the ban:

    def acceptable(self, tree: Expression) -> bool:
        if not is_valid_root(tree):
            return False
        if self.banned_substructures and (self.banned_substructures & one_layer_keys(tree)):
            return False

THE CONTRACT

A plugin is any importable module exposing `register_alphacube(ctx: PluginContext) -> None`. By the time it is called, `alphacube.operators` is imported but `build_registry` has NOT run, so the module's `@op(...)`-decorated kernels are already in `OPERATOR_REGISTRY` (that happens at import) and the registry build will pick them up, probes and all. Inside `register_alphacube` a plugin may:

- `ctx.register_scorer("partura", ParturaScorer)` -- a fitness name reachable from `--fitness partura`, `gp_params["fitness_kind"]` and the RL branch alike;
- do nothing else. Operators come from `@op` at import; generator hooks are passed per-miner through `gp_params`, not registered globally, because a hook is a property of one search run and a global registry of hooks would make two miners in one process interfere.

ORDERING, ENFORCED

    cli.main() -> plugins.load(args.plugin) -> args.fn(args) -> ... -> default_registry() -> build_registry()
                                                                                             ^ sets
                                                                      operators.common.registry_closed = True

After that point `op()` raises. The latch lives in `operators/common.py`, the module that owns `OPERATOR_REGISTRY`; `catalog` imports `operators`, so `catalog` setting the flag introduces no cycle. This is what replaces Partura's `catalog._DEFAULT = None` reset: there is nothing to reset because nothing was built yet.

For a library caller that does not go through the CLI (Partura's `scripts/idea_search.py`), the rule is the same: `alphacube.plugins.load(["partura.ac_plugin"])` must precede the first `parse()` / `default_registry()` / `run_mining()` call. `parser.parse`'s default argument path calls `default_registry()` lazily, so parsing a single seed expression first closes the registry -- which the latch now reports instead of silently dropping 45 operators.

THE FIELD / DAILY-FIELD NAMESPACE

`Registry` carries two disjoint name tuples and refuses an overlap at construction:

    Registry(fields=CUBE_FIELDS, constants=CONSTANTS, daily_fields=DAILY_LEAF_FIELDS)
      .fields        -> the 8 minute cube fields; read by parser.name, generator.fields (generator.py:78),
                        Vocabulary.fields (tokens.py:80), boosting.py:136, check_ban_key (gp.py:250)
      .daily_fields  -> the daily leaves; read ONLY by parser.name

That split is what keeps the two concerns separate: parsing and evaluating a daily field works everywhere by default, while SEARCH exposure requires a caller to pass `fields=`/`daily_fields=` explicitly. `len(registry)` counts operators only and is unchanged.

The boolean self-check becomes declarative rather than patched. Today Partura rebuilds the registry and then rewrites 9 base names' `OpSpec`s with `dataclasses.replace(sp, boolean_output=False, trivial_boolean=False)` (ops_ext.py:744-759), keyed off an externally maintained `NEW_OPERATORS` list and installed by monkeypatching the `build_registry` function object behind a `_partura` sentinel. After this change each kernel declares itself at its own definition site -- `@op("dt", "day", arity=1, real_valued=True)` -- and the probes are skipped rather than overridden, which also covers `coarse_output` (which the current patch leaves alone) and covers AlphaCube's own kernels (which the current patch, iterating `NEW_OPERATORS`, cannot reach).

The 9 Partura names to annotate, two distinct mechanisms, both confirmed empirically in the fact map:
  exact-equality ratios against continuous randn (ties essentially never occur, output collapses to one constant):
    day_flat_ratio, day_zero_ratio, day_flat_run_max, day_at_max_ratio, day_at_min_ratio,
    day_distinct_ratio, cross_flat_ratio
  decile bucketing with only 9 probe columns, so the kernel's own n>=2 validity gate never fires and the
  output is all-NaN:
    cs_bucket_demean, cs_bucket_zscore          (each also flagged on its nt_ twin -> 11 registry entries)

Plus AlphaCube's own `in_sustain_stddev` (operators/dt_in.py:832-843), whose first operand is semantically a {0,1} trigger mask: on continuous probe input `(x == 1).sum() == 0`, so `_get_rowwise_windows` finds no trigger row and the kernel returns an all-NaN tensor on every one of the four `_probe_constant_capable` families. That one is in a separate work package because fixing it CHANGES THE DEFAULT SEARCH VOCABULARY -- see backward_compat item 16.

risks: The _pick byte-identity is the design's weakest joint, and part of it is outside the design's control. The unweighted path keeps exactly two random.Random.choice calls in order, but `specs` order comes from `Registry.searchable()` = `self._ops.values()` = build_registry's INSERTION order. So a plugin whose kernels register in a different order, a new _VARIANT_DEFS entry, or a change to EXCLUDED_KERNELS silently changes every _pick result with no code change at all. The golden-key test makes it loud; nothing makes it impossible.

daily_only propagating by all() is a judgement call I may have wrong. `div(day_mean(Close), FloatCap)` is not daily_only, so `parse_legacy('day_sum(div(day_mean(Close), FloatCap)))')` stays legal and silently returns the identity. Switching to any() would close that but would also newly reject trees that are legal today (day_sum over a mixed collapsed subtree), breaking byte-identity for the legacy corpus. I chose byte-identity over completeness and this is the case where that choice shows.

Four live orientation conventions and no crash when you get one wrong. Raw parquet and tradability.board_limit are (D,S); the engine's internal panels dict is (S,D) (engine.py:151); EvalResult.panels is (D,S) via one .T (engine.py:196); P-round tensors are (D,S); cube-mode tensors are (A,B,1) with A/B meaning different axes per mode. A transpose bug produces a plausible panel with a plausible IC. The only defense is the non-square identifiable-value fixture, and it has to be non-square in the symbol-SUBSET case too (a 10-symbol view of a 10-symbol store is square again).

BoardCode is a type hole I am deliberately not closing. The shape system has no categorical type, so add(BoardCode, 1) is legal nonsense and cs_rank(BoardCode) is a 4-level staircase. LongScorer's min_distinct gate will reject most such factors but the ic/rank_ic fitness will not. I rejected a fifth Shape flag as out of proportion and rejected omitting the field because the research wants it; the mitigation is keeping it out of the GP leaf pool plus a docstring, which is a convention, not a type.

FloatShares may not exist. Only symbol / circulating_market_value / total_market_value were verified in daily_capital/*.parquet. The build script prints the real column list and omits the field rather than deriving it from back-adjusted prices, so the deliverable may be five fields, not six, and whoever runs it finds out on the server, not here.

A panel round holds the whole daily panel on device, and panel rounds have no byte budget at all. _chunk_sizes sizes only cube rounds; _run_panel_round runs on self.device with no accounting. One daily field is 40 MB, which is fine, but a tree using four of them in one P round holds four plus every computed panel. On a GPU with ALPHACUBE_GPU_FRACTION set that is a new unbudgeted allocation. The per-call cache released in evaluate()'s finally limits the lifetime, not the peak.

The plugin latch will fire on real code the first time. parser.parse's default argument path calls default_registry() lazily, so parsing one seed expression before loading the plugin closes the registry. cli.main() is ordered correctly, but a library caller -- which is exactly what Partura's scripts/idea_search.py is -- can easily parse seeds first. The latch converts a silent 45-missing-operators failure into a loud RuntimeError, which is the point, but the fix is a call-order change in Partura, not in AlphaCube, and it will look like a regression.

ListedDays from day_status cannot distinguish 'not yet listed' from 'the ingest missed this symbol'. SegmentedCubeStore.read_status fills uncovered cells with OUTSIDE_LIFECYCLE (store.py:381), so a symbol present in a segment but absent from the base reads as unlisted for the whole base range. That is correct for a genuinely new listing and wrong for an ingest gap, and the store alone cannot tell them apart. Any factor using ListedDays inherits that ambiguity.

accept_hook reproducibility is enforced by documentation only. hook_rng is provided and the hook's arity and return type are validated, but nothing stops a hook from touching gen._rng, re-entering the generator, or being stateful across calls. Partura's current hook does exactly the first of those; the migration fixes it, but the next hook author gets no help from the type system.

The scorer's `dates` are row-aligned with the panel, which means they include the warm-up rows. GPMiner passes list(view.dates) and the panels it scores are full-length (pipeline.run_mining trims only at reporting time, pipeline.py:447). A factory that assumes dates[0] == --start cuts its train/valid `trim` rows off (60 by default). The docstring says so; a silent off-by-60 is still the most likely way a plugin scorer goes wrong.

A rebuilt daily-field store does not invalidate the rank-ban exemplar cache. view_cache_key (rankban.py:242-249) hashes only dates[0], dates[-1], len(dates), n_symbols and the sample sizes -- it already cannot tell two stores with the same axes apart. I deliberately left it alone because changing it invalidates caches that cost ~2 hours to rebuild, so the operational rule is 'rebuild the daily fields -> run scripts/clean_exemplar_cache.py', and nothing enforces it.

WP-H6 is a real trajectory break with no clean lever, and I may be underestimating how much depends on the current vocabulary. Clearing in_sustain_stddev's flag grows searchable(include_boolean=False) by one, which shifts every _pick draw and every RL token index. Checkpoints, archives and the golden-key tests from WP-H2 all have to be regenerated. If any downstream comparison in docs/可交易回测.md assumes a fixed vocabulary across runs, this invalidates it.
